name: Encoder (structure to property)
question: Does the model read properties from structures correctly?
purpose: The label of every candidate, read from the returned structure, comes from this block, so its error is the floor on how precisely any target can be hit.
verdict_rule: the worst grade of its graded metrics

metrics.name: Target error relative to its spread
metrics.definition: Mean absolute error on materials with a non-zero target, divided by the standard deviation of that subset.
metrics.meaning_good: Labels are accurate enough to aim with: the fixed pipeline at 0.53 supports rho 0.98 end to end.
metrics.meaning_bad: The label error is comparable to the whole spread of the property, so a target cannot be aimed at.
metrics.remedy: More data, more epochs, or inspect label outliers.
metrics.recalibrated: The original band (0.25 / 0.50) graded every configuration FAIL, including the one that delivers rho 0.98, so it could not tell a working encoder from a broken one. Set from what is achievable and demonstrably sufficient, while still failing published (1.07) and control (1.99).

metrics.name: Target rank correlation
metrics.definition: Pearson r between predicted and true target on non-zero materials.
metrics.meaning_good: The ordering of materials by the property is right, which is what a search needs.
metrics.meaning_bad: The model cannot rank materials by the property.

metrics.name: Metal / non-metal accuracy
metrics.definition: Share of test materials on the right side of the zero-gap boundary.
metrics.meaning_good: The model distinguishes conductors from semiconductors, the coarsest and most important call.
metrics.meaning_bad: The model cannot tell a metal from a semiconductor, so any gap target is meaningless.
metrics.remedy: Switch the structure losses on (the control configuration shows their effect: 4% vs 98%).

metrics.name: Second property error relative to its spread
metrics.definition: Mean absolute error of the stability or energy property, divided by its standard deviation.
metrics.meaning_good: The stability estimate is usable for ranking.

metrics.name: Latent organised by property
metrics.definition: Error of a 5-nearest-neighbour prediction in the structure latent, divided by the property spread.
metrics.meaning_good: Materials with similar properties sit together in the latent, which is what makes a latent search possible.
metrics.meaning_bad: The latent is not organised by the property, so searching it cannot find the property.
metrics.remedy: More training, or check the alignment weight.
metrics.reference_note: The published app PASSES this while failing the property read-out: its latent was fine, its head was broken. That contrast is why these are separate metrics.

metrics.name: Trust outside the training chemistry
metrics.definition: Target error on materials containing a held-out element, divided by the error on seen chemistry.
metrics.meaning_good: Labels can be trusted for elements beyond the training set.
metrics.meaning_bad: Labels for materials containing new elements rest on untrained embeddings.
metrics.remedy: Keep candidates inside the training chemistry, or state the bias explicitly.
metrics.reference_note: Measured on SEPARATE models trained with La/Y held out, not on the configurations in the table, so no per-configuration value is stored: 2.9x, 3.1x and 3.4x worse (0.85 -> 2.50 eV, 0.86 -> 2.64, 0.79 -> 2.65). On Perov-5 this makes lanthanide labels run about 0.7 eV low. Capped at WARN because it bounds the SCOPE of a working encoder rather than showing a broken one; it only bites when the design space needs unseen elements, which on Perov-5 it always does (0 of 148 novel candidates avoided them).
